mission: Common area. Sera breaks the seal on the Codex case and every Force-sensitive in the room feels the artifact's resonance before anyone speaks. Ben touches the fragment; the experiential flash of unstructured Force lands as sensation, not paragraph. Four different reactions around the table.
why_now: Chapter 8's debate made the intellectual space. The Codex now provides the sensation that the concept alone could not -- this is where Ankhural's heresy stops being archive text and starts being something felt in the body.
conflict: The Codex's argument is devastating to hold as experience. If Ankhural was right about imposed structure at vergences, then a local moral certainty the Jedi have trusted may be something history built into a site rather than something the site revealed on its own. Four Force-users hold the same artifact and take four different readings from it. The scene does not confirm the theory; it confirms only how seductive it feels.
turning_point: Ben touches the Codex. For a handful of seconds the Force is present and unshaped — no direction, no texture, no moral register. His hand jerks back before his mind arrives.
opening_hook: The Codex fragment has been sealed in its case since the fortress. When Sera opens it, the air in the common area changes — everyone Force-sensitive feels the artifact's resonance simultaneously.
closing_hook: Ship alarm. The next planned stop — the Brotherhood Outpost — has been breached. Energy readings spiking. Someone is there, or has been there very recently.
emotional_trajectory: Intellectual engagement -> existential vertigo -> sharp alarm

stakes.personal: Ben's foundational understanding of the Force challenged at the deepest level
stakes.interpersonal: Four Force-sensitives experiencing the same artifact, interpreting it four different ways
stakes.external: The Codex provides the theoretical framework for understanding the wound — and for exploiting it

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — common area, the Codex fragment on the table between them
sensory_details: The Codex faintly lit inside its case; the experiential flash arriving as a sudden emptying — sound without body, weight without direction, the moral register gone from the Force and nothing replacing it; each character's Force presence reacting differently to the artifact
action_beats: Sera breaks the seal on the Codex case and lifts the fragment onto the common area table
Ben touches the Codex and his hand jerks back — the experiential flash of unstructured Force hitting like sensory overload
The ship alarm cuts through the discussion and Desh clears the common area to reach the cockpit in three seconds
promises_planted: The Codex's theoretical framework has a real-world answer (PP14)
notes: R06 is the intellectual center of the manuscript and the highest exposition-risk delivery in it. It must be received as sensation, not explained as narrator-endorsed conclusion. The flash of damaged, directionless Force is the first mild taste of what Ch13's full wound zone will deliver at scale -- keep this one mild and somatic. Use a somatic or acoustic vocabulary family (the emptying, the quick retreat, the body's refusal); do not use the handrail phrasing or the flat-note phrasing from earlier chapters. Diagnostic-voice trap -- Ben should not, in this scene, articulate the Codex's imposed-structure claim as settled truth. He feels the flash and pulls his hand back. Sera, Torin, and Kael take the ideas; Ben holds the experience. Anti-pattern: no character quotes the Codex at length -- it is received through reaction.
